subject: SOW fee apportionment & implementation window — redlines attached
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Julie Parker <julie.parker@novaapps.com>
Cc: Samir Khatri <samir.khatri@novaapps.com>
Date: 2027-08-01T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: SOW fee apportionment & implementation window - redlines attached

Hi Julie —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, we attached our proposed SOW v3 with two clean edits: (1) an apportionment of the initial integration fee across the first 12 months to match your budget cycle, and (2) a tighter implementation window to reflect the earlier cutover NovaApps requested.

High-level ask from our side: if you can confirm acceptance of the apportionment approach (split fee across 12 monthly invoices) we can keep the originally quoted unit price for Dedicated capacity but shift 20% of the integration line item into monthly billing. That avoids an up-front invoice surge for you.

What I need from you this week:
- Confirm that apportionment is acceptable to procurement
- Confirm the revised go-live window: target 2027-10-15 (with a 2-week buffer)

Attachment: NovaApps_SOW_v3_redline.docx (docx)

If that works I will loop in legal to finalize a Change Order and get it on DocuSign.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter | Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1-415-555-0132

From: Julie Parker <julie.parker@novaapps.com>

Cc: Samir Khatri <samir.khatri@novaapps.com>, procurement@novaapps.com
Date: 2027-08-02T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOW fee apportionment & implementation window - redlines attached

Ben —

Thanks for the doc and the clear options. Procurement did a quick review and a few notes before we can commit:

- Apportionment sounds acceptable in principle, but procurement requires a one-line statement confirming there is no interest charge or finance fee applied when the integration fee is spread across invoices.
- We need the implementation window moved two weeks later (target go-live 2027-10-29) because a dependent internal platform team has a freeze the week of 10/10.
- We cannot accept any new SLA credit structure that reduces existing credits; any change to SLA credits must be revenue-neutral.

I copied Samir and procurement. If legal at Redwood can confirm the no-finance-fee line and preserve the SLA credits, we can run our final internal approval and aim to sign the CO next week.

Team —

Forwarding Julie's procurement response. They asked for three narrow confirmations:
1) No finance/interest fees applied to the apportionment
2) Move go-live to 2027-10-29 (2-week shift)
3) SLA credits to remain revenue-neutral (no net reduction)

My recommendation: we accept #1 and #2; for #3 propose an equivalent credit reconciliation (i.e., keep existing credit structure, and if we add additional credits for new commitments, offset via a defined cap so it stays revenue-neutral). Laura — can you confirm finance is OK with the apportionment treatment (no fees)? Rishi — can legal draft a 1-page change order with: apportionment language, updated go-live date, and a short SLA-credit-preservation clause? Grace — please prepare an updated order form showing the amortized integration line across 12 months for NovaApps' AP team.

Timing: Julie would like to sign next week if we can produce a clean CO and a DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Ben

Ben / team —

Thanks for the clear asks. Legal has prepared a short Change Order draft and a PDF redline for internal review. Summary of what we've accepted and how we'll phrase it: 

- Fee apportionment: we will add a single sentence to the Change Order that the integration fee will be invoiced in twelve equal monthly installments, with no interest, finance charges, or early-payment penalties applied as a result of the split.
- Go-live date: updated to target 2027-10-29 with a 2-week buffer; implementation milestones remain unchanged except for the adjusted target.
- SLA credits: we will include a preservation clause stating "Redwood will not reduce pre-existing SLA credit entitlements as a result of this Change Order; any additional credits arising from new commitments will be offset by a cap to ensure net revenue neutrality." Please note this preserves customer-facing credits while protecting the company from open-ended liability.
